solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former lover writes story about European businessman's fund

indicators.note: about here places the story around, next to, the European letter, so the story follows it

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
pens is a verb meaning writes
an account is a story or narrative

explanation.surface: A jilted ex writes a kiss-and-tell piece about a Continental tycoon's money.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance a company gives an employee for business costs, so it is a fund for a businessman.

clue.text: Instrument to sharpen provided after axes cut

indicators.note: after places the sharpening word behind the other pieces

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph
to lop is to cut off
to hone is to sharpen a blade

explanation.surface: A tool that needs sharpening once the axes have been used for cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' looks like the chopping tools that need sharpening, but it means the x and y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument with wooden bars struck by mallets.

clue.text: More is unknown locked into variable rate

indicators.note: locked into means one piece is shut inside the other
variable suggests the letters of rate are not fixed in place and can be rearranged

parts.note: x is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: More of an unknown quantity is tied into a fluctuating interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' anagrams RATE to E-TRA, and 'locked into' puts X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, so it is a synonym for more.

clue.text: Count firm implements periodically

parts.note: the whole clue describes a business regularly counting the goods and equipment it holds

explanation.surface: An instruction to tally up a company's tools at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocktaking is the periodic counting of the goods and materials a business has on hand.

clue.text: Venue taking a period of time to erect

indicators.note: to erect is to put upright, so in this down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A building site that takes a long time to put up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to erect' reads AN ERA from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place where events, sports or concerts are staged.

clue.text: Three short men dance

indicators.note: short means each man is cut off before his final letter
three asks for the man word written out three times in a row

parts.note: a chap is a man, and the clue asks for three of them
a chap is a man; this is the third of the three men the clue asks for

explanation.surface: Three little men break into a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three' means the shortened man appears three times in a row, so the same piece is used once more after the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Join male leaving in minute, hurriedly

indicators.note: hurriedly suggests the remaining letters are thrown together in a rush and rearranged
leaving means the male letter departs from the word minute

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to join up after a man leaves at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes M from MINUTE, giving INUTE, which 'hurriedly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring or come together, a synonym for join.

clue.text: Volunteers to receive new vehicles

definitions.meaning: to volunteer something is to offer it, as one offers a bid or resignation
a tender is a vehicle or vessel that supplies another, like a railway coal truck or a ship's boat

explanation.surface: People offering their help to take delivery of a new fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: offers, and supply vehicles; 'to receive new' only links the two, as tenders are invited when new vehicles are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenders are both offers put forward and support craft that carry supplies to a larger vessel or engine.

clue.text: Sheep and dog quickly advance

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene of a sheep and dog moving forward fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp up is to increase production or effort rapidly.

clue.text: Assign everyone with books

parts.note: all means everyone
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Handing out reading material to the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to give out a share to someone, a synonym for assign.

clue.text: Couples regularly share control

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of the word Couples

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Couples routinely split the duties of running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation means the working or running of something, as in a machine under control.

clue.text: Encouraging chat kept pal excited

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of kept pal are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A rousing talk kept a friend fired up.
explanation.definitionFit: A short speech meant to motivate or boost morale.

clue.text: Without cases, pack this? Never manage

indicators.note: without cases means each word loses its outer letters, the way contents are taken out of their cases

explanation.surface: A traveller doubts they can pack this without suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without cases' strips PACK, THIS and NEVER to AC, HI and EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to succeed in doing it, a synonym for manage.

clue.text: Expert university head in Durham standing out

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert

indicators.note: head in means the first letter of the word Durham

explanation.surface: A specialist heads up a university department in Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a university city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean projecting above a surface, as a nail stands proud of wood.

clue.text: Muck-raker's rubbish transported to the north

definitions.note: the possessive reads as muck-raker is, with is as the link

indicators.note: to the north means upwards, so in this down clue the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
carted means carried or transported

explanation.surface: A scandal-monger's junk is hauled up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' reverses ROT CARTED, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A muck-raker digs up scandal to disparage people, as a detractor belittles them.

clue.text: In usual way, sitting in sofa, sitcom essential

indicators.note: sitting in suggests the letters are seated inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lounging on the sofa is the essential way to watch a sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something as it comes means accepting it in its ordinary state, without special arrangement.

clue.text: Area of London containing heath — no it's Barking

indicators.note: containing means the scrambled letters wrap around the heath plant
barking means mad, so the letters of no it's go crazy and rearrange

parts.note: ling is heather, the plant of the heath

explanation.surface: A disagreement over which London district has a heath: not this one, it's Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is itself an area of east London, a decoy for the definition; here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough in north London.

clue.text: Peculiarity of chap raised alarm with maiden

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in this down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a siren is an alarm
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A man's odd habit of raising the alarm whenever a young woman appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannerism is a distinctive habit or quirk of behaviour, so a peculiarity.

clue.text: Crackers we see, and malt type of biscuits

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: We look at crackers and some malted biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like biscuits in a list of biscuits; it is the anagram signal. Sweetmeal biscuits are British digestives made with wholemeal flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetmeal is a kind of sweetened wholemeal biscuit, as in a digestive.

clue.text: Scaffolder at top, one making tiles break

indicators.note: at top means the first letter of Scaffolder, at the top of this down entry

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat, so a hatter makes them

explanation.surface: A scaffolder up high and a roofer cause roof tiles to break.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is an old slang word for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces.

clue.text: Woman turned no good, in the main

indicators.note: turned means the whole is read the other way round
in places the no good letters inside the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: A woman who went bad while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic name for the open sea; 'turned' reverses SENGA, the sea with no good inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Dog beginning to show character with lead removed

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word show
with lead removed means the front letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A dog starts to show its true nature once taken off its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with lead removed' drops the L of LETTER, leaving ETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gundog, such as the Irish or English setter.

clue.text: Week in a hospital room is not comfortable

indicators.note: in places the week abbreviation inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: A week spent on a hospital ward is not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means causing unease or embarrassment, so not at ease.

clue.text: Adopted lower position untangling anklet, releasing article

indicators.note: untangling suggests the remaining letters are straightened out into a new order
releasing means the article letter is let go from the word anklet

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone crouched down to untangle an ankle bracelet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing' takes A from ANKLET, leaving NKLET for 'untangling' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling means lowering oneself onto the knees, so taking a lower posture.

clue.text: Perfect daughter about in the morning

parts.note: re means about or concerning
AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A proud parent talks of a perfect daughter in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, dream means ideal, as in a dream holiday.

clue.text: Relative rejected whiskey to consume a piece of cake

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the relative is reversed

parts.note: a son is a relative
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A family member refused whisky but agreed to eat some cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for something very easy to do.

clue.text: Hoard stone and timber

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
ash is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: A stockpile of building materials, stone and wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a secret store of something, so a hoard.

clue.text: Use cashpoint in plane, perhaps, not empty

indicators.note: in puts the cash machine inside the tree

parts.note: the plane is a kind of tree, signalled by perhaps
ATM is a cash machine, a cashpoint in Britain

indicators.note: empty means the word not loses its middle, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Withdrawing cash on an aircraft, as long as the account is not empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way something is handled or used.

clue.text: Privately like one editor to return

parts.note: as means like
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the editor letters are reversed

explanation.surface: Speaking privately, like an editor waiting for someone to return.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said aside is said privately, out of others' hearing.

clue.text: Residence for elderly with space to occupy roughly thirteen more

indicators.note: to occupy means the space goes inside the scrambled letters
roughly suggests the letters of thirteen more are roughly put together in new order

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

explanation.surface: An old people's home with room for thirteen more residents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' anagrams THIRTEEN MORE, and 'to occupy' puts EM inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A care home where older people live after leaving work.
